background.title: Reserve Bank of India
background.extract: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of the Republic of India. It was established on April 1, 1935 by the British Raj, with enactment of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. Although, the RBI is owned by the Government of India, the RBI is an autonomous regulatory organisation for the Indian banking & financial system with exercising substantial amount of independance and power over the Indian Economy. It is responsible for the issue, supply and control of the Indian rupee. It also manages the country's main payment systems & the foreign exchange under the FEMA Act, 1999.

places.title: India
places.extract: India, officially the Republic of India, is a country in South Asia. It is the world's seventh-largest country by area and its most populous. Bounded by the Indian Ocean on the south, the Arabian Sea on the southwest, and the Bay of Bengal on the southeast, it shares land borders with Pakistan to the west, China, Nepal, and Bhutan to the north, and Bangladesh and Myanmar to the east. In the Indian Ocean, India is near Sri Lanka and the Maldives.
